records.deidentified_narrative: units 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 [roadway] of i-20. a traffic hazard developed ahead of them from a dog entering the roadway and a pedestrian that had parked her vehicle (unit 7) in the center median at a break in the barrier with posted sign saying the use of that portion of the median is for official or emergency vehicle use only. the driver of unit 1 may have been following too closely and he failed to control his speed. unit 1 struck the back right of unit 2 with unit 1's front left and then also appears to have struck the back right of unit 3 as it was deflected to the right and unit 2 to the left - into the concrete barrier. unit 2 [roadway]/pushed against the center median concrete barrier - left front quarter damage. broken glass from the back window of unit 2 was thrown into the bed of unit 3 during the collision. unit 3 was pushed into the back end of unit 4. the driver of unit 4 may have been following too closely to unit 5 and he failed to control his speed or was pushed into the back end of unit 5. unit 5 sustained mostly back distributed damage and was pushed into the towing hitch of unit 6. unit 6 did not appear to have sustained any damage. there may have been one more vehicle that did not stop and made contact with unit 3 and caused it slight side swipe damage - [roadway] - on unit 3's right back quarter, above its rear right tire ( from the 5 o'clock position). unit 4 also had side swipe damage to its left back quarter (from the 11-o'clock position) that may have been caused by side swiping the right front quarter ( from the 5-o'clock position) of unit 2 - bumper pushed forward. unit 2 did not appear to have struck any vehicle in front of it as there was no evidence of front end damage caused from in front of it. the pedestrian left the scene of this crash prior to my arrival but she called the van zandt county dispatcher to give her information and to say that the dog had caused the crash. the pedestrian also stated via cellphone communication to me that she had left the scene of the crash because several men had confronted her aggressively and she felt threatened at the location. the pedestrian also told me that initially she had seen the dog on the roadway as she traveled westbound and she drove to the eastbound side to park in the median to try to help the dog. no witnesses to this crash that had not been in vehicles that sustained damage stopped to give information.

records.public_safe_text: on march 10th, 2025 at approximately 1353 hours i, officer s bear (#1189) and wilmer medical unit #461 were dispatched to carmax auto auctions located at [roadway]. wilmer, dallas county texas 75172 for a pedestrian struck by a vehicle. the struck individual was unable to stand, with limited verbal communication with medical personnel. he was transported [medical facility] with unknown injuries. there were no immediate indicators of major injury or brain trauma. the individual was employed by another dealership and walking west-northwest across the parking / vehicle staging area. the driver operating unit 1 was sub-contracted under another vehicle dealership staging vehicles for pick-up. while moving the vehicle the driver disregarded the areas directional travel lanes driving west between parked vehicles, then making a u-turn within the parking area to park the vehicle. unit 1 struck the pedestrian at low speed with the front right quarter panel area striking the pedestrian in the back of the legs causing him to fall. unit 1 did not receive any damage. the staging area is designated as east travel only for vehicle traffic, with regular foot traffic. the driver stated to have been aware of the pedestrian, believing him to be at a safe distance and to have been looking towards his intended parking spot, and not in front of the vehicle. the incident was captured on video surveillance by carmax. an incident report ([identifier]) was created to include this footage and all employer information for the record. nothing further.

records.deidentified_narrative: austin police initiated a traffic stop on a maroon buick [roadway]., but the driver of unit #1 evaded their lawful detention. the police disengaged from the pursuit due to heavy pedestrian and vehicular traffic. shortly after, officers arrived at the scene of a collision not far from the evasion, involving the same maroon buick (unit #1) that had previously evaded the stop. they observed that unit #1 had collided with units #2 and #3 before leaving the roadway, going onto a sidewalk, and crashing into a fence line at [roadway]. the vehicle then struck a tree on its right side and came to a complete stop. police reported that the driver and a passenger exited unit #1 and immediately fled the scene, jumping fences and heading south into the adjacent neighborhood. the driver of unit #2 stated he was traveling east in the [roadway]. when he was aggressively struck from behind by unit #1, forcing him off the roadway and onto the sidewalk and easement. the driver of unit #3 reported that she was also traveling east in the same area when her vehicle was struck on the right side, causing her to temporarily lose control before coming to a stop. it is believed that unit #1 first struck unit #2, then collided with unit #3 before leaving the roadway and crashing into a fence and a tree. a pedestrian walking east along the south curb line reported hearing the crash unfold and saw unit #1 heading in his direction. he immediately ran south and jumped the fence to avoid being struck, as unit #1 traveled parallel to him on the right side, placing him between the vehicle and the fence. the pedestrian was struck by the vehicle, resulting in minor injuries.

records.public_safe_text: unit 1 was traveling eastbound on the beach at beach barrel 81, [roadway]. unit 2 is a 6 yoa boy playing on the beach near his father and grandfather. the child was struck by the front bumper of the truck in the back of his head and fell to the ground. the father, grandfather, and driver of unit 1 did not see the accident or realize it had occurred. the child returned to their beach house at 860 meyning to seek help from his mother. a beach worker called 911. when i spoke with the child he advised the vehicle was a gray pickup. no other information was available. ems checked the child and located a small laceration to the back of his head which had stopped bleeding. the child was transported by ambulance to utmb as a precaution and for stitches. while speaking with the ems crew the driver of unit 1 returned to the scene and stated that an unknown person had flagged him down and told him he had struck a child. driver of unit 1 stated he searched the beach and then saw our lights. driver of unit 1 stated that he never saw the child or realized he had hit him. the driver of unit 1 was not impaired. deputy j. danesi performed sfsts on driver of unit 1 and he passed without issue.
